How to choose a red light therapy manufacturer in China

Choose a manufacturing partner by matching its product platform, evidence and delivery terms to your brand’s requirements.

By APTREDLIGHT · 4 November 2026 · Manufacturer-authored procurement guide

Start with the product you intend to sell

A panel, a flexible mat and a full-body wrap require different materials, assembly methods, packaging and evaluation plans. Define your intended use, destination market, target specification and expected order volume before comparing factories.

Compare six things before choosing a supplier

DecisionAsk the manufacturerWhat to compare
Manufacturing scopeWhich stages are performed in-house? Can we review the relevant production process?Business identity, facility information and responsibility for assembly and inspection.
Product configurationWhat is the exact model and version quoted?Wavelengths, LED arrangement, electrical input power, controls, dimensions and accessories.
Measured performanceHow was output measured?Distance, meter, operating mode, measurement positions and test conditions.
DocumentationWhich documents cover this exact configuration?Model identification, report scope, issuing body and the intended destination market.
CustomizationWhat changes are included and what requires development?Logo, housing, software, packaging, sample approval and ownership of custom work.
Commercial termsWhat is included in the delivered order?MOQ, sample cost, packaging, inspection, lead time, shipping terms and written warranty.

OEM or ODM: choose the scope before the price

For an existing product platform, begin with branding and the available configuration options. For a more substantial design change, agree on feasibility, development fees, milestones and sample acceptance before production. Suppliers use OEM and ODM differently, so record the actual deliverables in writing.

Where APTREDLIGHT fits your shortlist

APTREDLIGHT offers China-based red light therapy product development and manufacturing for brands, distributors and wellness businesses. Explore T300 panels, full-body panels, portable panels, mats and wraps. Available customization depends on the selected platform.

Use the same evaluation criteria for APTREDLIGHT and every other supplier. Request the specification and available supporting documents for your exact project.

OEM/ODM BUYER GUIDE

How to choose a red light therapy OEM/ODM manufacturer

An evidence-first sourcing checklist for brands and importers.

Evaluate manufacturers on more than prices, LED counts or brochure specifications. Specify the intended product and market first, then match supplier claims to the exact model being ordered.

1. Define your use case and target market

Describe the form factor: desktop panel, full-body panel, flexible mat or sleeping bag. Include target customer, intended claims, order quantity, shipping destination and app or control requirements. Consumer wellness products and regulated medical devices may have different obligations.

2. Verify optical specifications

Request the measured spectrum, wavelength allocation, center and average irradiance at a defined distance, coverage area, measurement equipment and test method. Distinguish electrical input wattage from optical irradiance. Confirm the actual configuration of each SKU.

3. Verify destination-market safety documentation

Request electrical, EMC, photobiological, chemical and labeling documents applicable to the model and market. FDA establishment registration is not equivalent to FDA clearance or approval; CE marking does not independently verify every product. Use qualified compliance advice for intended claims.

4. Define private-label and quality requirements

Confirm material, finish, housing, firmware and controller customization, branding, packaging, manuals, sample approval, traceability, in-process checks, final inspection, warranty and change control.

5. Compare suppliers consistently

AreaEvidence to request
OpticsSpectrum, irradiance method, test distance, treatment coverage
Electrical and safetyModel-specific test reports, power ratings, thermal tests
CustomizationMOQ, approved artwork, tooling scope, samples
QualityInspection plan, batch traceability, change control
CommercialIncoterms, lead time, spare parts, warranty process

6. Approve samples before scale-up

Test samples against a signed specification and retain reference units. For EU and UK buyers, confirm applicable labeling, importer requirements and safety documentation before printing final artwork.

What to verify before your first red light therapy OEM sample

A useful sample order begins with an agreed specification. Give every supplier the same brief so your comparison leads to a clear purchasing decision.

1. Identify the exact version

Record the model name, wavelength list, LED layout, controller version, accessories and packaging. Ask whether your sample matches the version proposed for bulk production. A shared product name alone does not define a configuration.

2. Make output measurements comparable

Request the measurement distance, meter model, operating mode, measurement positions and test conditions alongside irradiance results. Keep electrical input power, nominal LED ratings and measured optical output in separate fields. Figures collected under different conditions should not be treated as equivalent.

3. Evaluate the experience and documentation

Review controls, mounting, packaging, labels and the instructions supplied with the sample. Request documents that identify the exact model and configuration. Record any unavailable evidence as an open item before your purchasing decision.

4. Put commercial terms in writing

Confirm sample charges, customization scope, minimum quantities, lead time, delivery terms and warranty responsibilities. Agree how specification changes will be approved and how the production order will be inspected.

A brief you can send to APTREDLIGHT

“We are developing a private-label red light therapy product for [market]. Our preferred format is [panel / portable / mat / wrap], with an initial quantity of [quantity]. Please confirm available configurations, customization scope, sample terms, measurement reports and model-specific documentation.”

Red Light Therapy OEM Repeat Orders: A Buyer’s Guide to Change Control

An approved sample is a reference point. A repeat order needs a clear record of what stays the same, what changes and who approves the difference.

For brands buying red light therapy panels, mats or wraps for the US, UK, Europe and Australia, a repeat purchase can involve a new destination, revised packaging or a different controller. Treat each change as an explicit decision before production. This guide outlines a practical purchasing workflow to discuss with APTREDLIGHT; it does not claim that every product already has the same documentation package.

1. Create an approved configuration record

Give the accepted configuration a revision number and approval date. Keep the physical sample identifier, written specification and artwork files together. A phrase such as “same as last time” leaves room for different interpretations when a team member, destination or component changes.

RecordWhat to identifyWhat the buyer checks
Product and light configurationExact model, version, agreed wavelength layout and operating modes.The repeat-order specification refers to the approved version.
Controls and powerController or firmware revision where applicable, input specification and supplied plug or adapter.Any proposed substitution is listed before production.
Mechanical parts and accessoriesHousing finish, mounting parts, stand, cables and included items.Fit, included quantities and assembly instructions match the order.
Brand materialsLabel, manual, carton and insert file revisions.Approved languages, model references and artwork are consistent.
Acceptance evidenceAgreed inspection criteria, measurement conditions and report references.Records identify the configuration and batch being reviewed.

2. Ask for a change proposal before accepting a substitution

If a component or packaging material becomes unavailable, request the current item, proposed replacement, reason for the change and affected orders. Ask what evaluation is needed and whether previously supplied documents still cover the revised configuration. Do not assume that a visually similar part is interchangeable.

For an optical configuration change, request comparable measurement conditions. For a controller change, agree which functions will be checked. For packaging changes, review product protection, included accessories and the updated packing arrangement. These are purchasing review points, not a universal test protocol.

3. Use a short approval sequence

  1. Describe: document the proposed change and the baseline revision.
  2. Review: identify affected functions, instructions, packaging and supporting evidence.
  3. Verify: agree any revised sample, targeted evaluation or document review needed.
  4. Approve: record the buyer’s decision, date and new revision.
  5. Identify: specify the first order or batch using the approved change.

Keep pending changes separate from released specifications. If approval is incomplete, explicitly agree how the affected production will be handled rather than allowing assumptions to become order instructions.

4. Separate destination versions

A brand selling into several countries may need different plugs, packaging languages, instructions or labeling arrangements. Define destination variants under separate SKU or revision references. Confirm the exact configuration and available documentation for each market with the responsible parties before release; a successful order for one destination does not establish suitability for every destination.

5. Close the loop at shipment and receiving

Request a shipment record linking the purchase order, product revision, batch identifier, packed quantity and agreed inspection documents. On receipt, compare a selected unit and its accessories, labels and packaging with that record. Report discrepancies with clear photographs and identifiers so both teams discuss the same unit and revision.

For replacement accessories or after-sales parts, include the affected product revision. Ask the supplier to confirm compatibility rather than relying only on the model name.

A repeat-order message you can use

We plan to reorder [model] against approved specification [revision/date] and previous order [reference], for [destination]. Please confirm the configuration, accessories, artwork and packing remain as approved. List any proposed changes separately, with the reason, evaluation required and first affected batch. Please confirm quantity, lead time and the shipment records available for this order.

Questions before you reorder

Does the same model name guarantee the same configuration?

No. Ask for a revision identifier covering the agreed hardware, controls, accessories and packaging. A model name or product photograph alone does not establish that two orders are identical.

Should every change require a new sample?

Agree a review process based on the change. Ask the manufacturer to explain the affected functions, documents and verification needs; record whether a revised sample or targeted evaluation is required before approval.

What should we send APTREDLIGHT for a repeat order?

Send the previous order reference, approved specification revision, destination market, required quantity and requested changes. Ask for written confirmation of unchanged items and a separate list of proposed changes.

Compare the complete configuration

Red light therapy OEM/ODM sourcing FAQ

Practical answers for brand owners, wholesalers and sourcing teams. Prepared by APTREDLIGHT using the product scope and sourcing workflow published on this website.

What does APTREDLIGHT supply?

APTREDLIGHT presents red light therapy panels, portable and desktop formats, full-body equipment, LED masks, mats and sleeping bags for B2B OEM/ODM sourcing. Its website and official Alibaba showroom provide two inquiry paths. Confirm the exact model and order terms with the supplier.

How should I compare panels, masks and mats?

Start with the intended format and user setting. For panels, compare placement, mounting and documented coverage. For masks, compare fit, contact materials and instructions. For flexible mats and sleeping bags, compare dimensions, cleaning, controller functions and packing. Format alone does not establish optical output or suitability for an intended use.

What is the difference between OEM and ODM sourcing?

OEM commonly refers to manufacturing to an agreed buyer specification; ODM commonly refers to adapting a supplier-developed design. Terminology varies by contract. Specify design ownership, permitted changes, tooling ownership and change-control responsibilities in writing.

What should an OEM quotation request include?

Include your destination market, product format or model, estimated quantity, wavelength requirements, electrical input, packaging artwork, labeling and manual needs, sample expectations and launch schedule. Ask for itemized sample, tooling, packaging, testing and shipping costs where applicable.

How can buyers compare irradiance claims?

Ask each supplier for the measurement distance, instrument, operating mode, measurement grid, center reading and average across the stated area. Numbers collected using different distances or methods are not directly comparable. Request model-specific supporting records.

Are MOQ, lead time and certifications the same for every model?

No universal values are published on this site. Request a written offer for the exact configuration, quantity and destination market. Check that any certificate or test report covers that model and intended use; a supplier-level statement does not establish product approval.

How can I contact APTREDLIGHT?

Use the request-a-quote page, WhatsApp at +86 188 2343 5519 or the official APTREDLIGHT Alibaba showroom. The website inquiry form prepares a WhatsApp message; you must send that message in WhatsApp to deliver your inquiry.

Which products can I source from APTREDLIGHT?

Explore red light panels, portable devices, LED masks, flexible mats, sleeping bags, wraps, caps and full-body systems. The current catalog is a starting point; request the exact model sheet and available options for your project.

Can you put our brand on the products?

Logo placement, product finish, labels, manuals, accessories and packaging can be discussed for your selected platform. Send your artwork needs and order plan so the team can confirm scope and MOQ.

What is the minimum order quantity?

MOQ varies with the platform and customization scope. Sample orders, logo customization, special packaging and new tooling may have different requirements. Request a quotation for your exact configuration.

Can we evaluate a sample before placing a bulk order?

Ask for current sample availability, pricing and shipping for your selected model. Agree on the sample configuration and acceptance checklist before evaluating it for a production order.

Which wavelengths and controls can we request?

Use the configuration studio to outline your preferred wavelengths and controls. Selections are development requests; compatibility, component availability and model-specific options must be confirmed with APTREDLIGHT.

How should we compare irradiance figures?

Request the measurement distance, meter, operating mode, measurement positions and units together with the exact product version. Center and average readings should be identified separately.

Which technical documents should we request?

Start with the model specification, user manual, electrical ratings, optical measurements and available safety reports. Request the documents relevant to your exact configuration, intended use and destination before confirming product claims.

What affects production lead time?

The selected platform, component availability, quantity, sample revisions, artwork approval and tooling scope all affect timing. Include your target launch date in the project brief and confirm the schedule in your quotation.

Can we visit the factory in Shenzhen?

Contact APTREDLIGHT to arrange a visit to our Shiyan, Bao’an, Shenzhen location. Share your travel dates, product interests and meeting agenda so the team can confirm the arrangements.

How do we request an OEM/ODM quotation?

Your technical verification checklist

Ask our team to confirm availability and scope for each item. This is a procurement checklist, not a claim that every report is available for every configuration.

  • Manufacturer identity and the production stages performed in-house.
  • Exact wavelength list, LED arrangement and independent channel options.

APTREDLIGHT · OEM / ODM SOURCING

Technical documentation for your OEM project

Build your sourcing decision around the exact device you plan to order.

This page explains what to request from our team. It is not a certificate repository or a statement that every report is available for every product. Availability and scope must be confirmed for the selected model.

1. Product configuration sheet

Request the model and revision, wavelength list, LED layout, dimensions, electrical input power, controls, accessories, packaging and manual. Identify any differences between the evaluation sample and the proposed production version.

2. Performance measurement record

Ask for irradiance in mW/cm² with the measurement distance, instrument, operating mode, positions and test conditions. Separate electrical input power from LED nominal ratings and measured optical output. For temperature, noise, flicker or EMF figures, ask for the measurement method and conditions.

3. Model-specific supporting documents

Share your destination market and intended product use. Request available reports and declarations with matching model identifiers, versions and scope. Resolve any gaps before approving the order or making claims on your own product listing.

4. Production and acceptance plan

Agree on the approved sample, configuration change control, inspection criteria, aging-test scope, traceability, packaging checks and pre-shipment review. Put the agreed requirements into the purchase specification.

5. Written commercial terms

Confirm sample and bulk pricing, minimum quantities, development fees, lead time, included accessories, delivery terms, warranty coverage and responsibility for after-sales handling.

Send a focused document request

Include your model, target market, intended use, customization and order quantity. Our team can confirm which materials are available and which items need further evaluation.
